title: OzoneBank incident retro + mitigation roadmap
summary: Postmortem-style checkin for the recent degradation where a KV cache eviction cascade increased token latency and caused partial failover to fallback models. Reviewed root causes, short-term mitigations, and a phased pilot for Dedicated/Private routing. Action owners and bench plan agreed.
topics: VPC / private deployment concerns and peering
KMS/HSM rotation, audit logs, SOC2 evidence
action_items: Diego Martinez: run full peak bench (24h spike, 50k reqs) and share raw csv + summary: due 2026-04-30
Liam O'Reilly: provide production traces (relevant spans) and request IDs for the 2026-04-14 incident: due 2026-04-25
Samira Khan: share security pack (SOC2 attestation, KMS notes, RBAC guide) and pricing for a 3-week Dedicated pilot: due 2026-04-26
Priya Nandakumar: confirm legal/contract timeline and decide on pilot procurement path: due 2026-05-03
next_steps: Schedule bench kickoff (Redwood SE + OzoneBank SRE): 2026-04-27 10:00 UTC
Redwood to provide updated fallback policy config example and canary plan
Customer to spin up a VPC peering test cluster and share connectivity notes
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-23 15:00 UTC | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Liam (OzoneBank SRE), Priya (Head of Platform), Marcus (Security)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight. 15-20 minute retro, then ops plan and next steps. liam, can you give the quick recap from your side?

[00:34] Liam: yeah thanks. so on Apr 14th we saw a latency uptick, tokens per request went up about 3x, a few zones saw evictions in the KV cache which cascaded, we fell back to smaller model variants and that pushed up tail latency. key point: it wasn't a single node it was a churn event.

[01:08] Diego: when you say evictions, do you mean prefix KV eviction or full KV flush?

[01:13] Liam: mostly prefix - we think some large prefix keys bumped the cache out, also noticed a pattern of concurrent cold-starts reheating the warmers. logs show a bunch of cache misses at the same time.

[02:02] Priya: and that triggered our own autoscaling to spin up more instances but we saw request piling because the model load added overhead, right? we had warmup lag.

[02:20] Marcus: also to note, our security team flagged we couldn't easily correlate some of the request IDs to the audit logs during the window - there was an ingestion blip in our log pipeline.

[03:01] Samira: yup. ok so two threads: reliability (KV/cache + warmup) and observability (request ids / tracing). we pushed the initial mitigations last week (changed cache TTLs, bumped prefix limits). results?

[03:30] Liam: it helped but didn't eliminate the tail. still seeing rare 95/99 spikes on long prompts.

[04:05] Diego: did you have prefix caching turned on with continuous batching? was batching size spiky?

[04:12] Liam: batching was enabled but had lots of variance. i think the runtime merged requests inefficiently under the spike - maybe the kernel choices for those sequences weren't optimal.

[05:00] Diego: (murmur) yeah we've seen that when sequence-length distribution is bimodal. runtime picks kernels for avg case and then mis-schedules.

[06:04] Priya: given that, what are the near-term controls? we need something we can ship before contract renewal.

[06:20] Samira: short-term: tighten prefix eviction thresholds, force sticky routing for hot prefixes to same pool, and add a temporary model-size prioritization to avoid falling to the smallest variant unnecessarily. medium-term: Dedicated pilot with pinned capacity and controlled autoscale. long-term: Private deployment or Dedicated depending on results.

[07:05] Marcus: for Private we need KMS details and HSM integration, also audit log retention and proof material for SOC2 and ISO. can you share specifics?

[07:30] Samira: yes, i'll share the security pack. it's got SOC2 attestation, KMS integration guide, HSM notes, and our RBAC + audit logs section. Diego, can you prepare a short note on how fallbacks are auditable?

[08:10] Diego: sure - i'll include where fallback decisions are logged (route decision id, model id, reason code) and how to tie that to request ids. note: sometimes the transcriber/mgmt layer mashes IDs - we'll recommend passing a consistent client request id.

[09:00] Liam: action: we'll find trace spans around the 14th. we have some samples but need guidance on which request ids to pull.

[09:20] Samira: Diego, can you propose the bench plan? we need to prove both steady-state and burst behaviour.

[09:35] Diego: plan is a 24-48h bench with a 1hr cold-start spike, then sustained 1k RPS for 3 hours, then a 30m 10k RPS spike. we'll capture latency, eviction stats, kernel selection traces, and model fallback counts. will share spreadsheet and raw CSV.

[10:12] Priya: will that simulate our true prompt distribution? we have many long conversational prompts and also embeddings calls mixed in.

[10:24] Diego: yes we'll seed with a sampled distribution from your traces; we'll mask PII. we might mis-transcribe some tokens in the bench but should be fine.

[11:00] Marcus: security question: during Dedicated pilot, who has access to logs and key material? we need SSO + SAML, RBAC to ensure only select engineers can see raw traces.

[11:30] Samira: we support SSO/SAML, attribute-based RBAC, and can limit log retention. for Dedicated we provide a dedicated GPU pool and optional private control plane in a VPC so raw data never leaves your network.

[12:20] Priya: peering: we need instructions for cross-account VPC peering with our cloud provider, and any firewall rules.

[12:40] Diego: we'll send a connectivity checklist. note that IP rotation during autoscale can break peering if filters are strict; recommend CIDR-based rules and a stable NAT egress for control-plane callbacks.

[13:15] Liam: on the observability side, the ingestion blip - we suspect an upstream log forwarder OOMed. that's on our side but made triage slower.

[14:00] Samira: ok understood. let's map responsibilities so nothing slips.

[14:25] (silence / note taking)

[15:00] Diego: quick note on fallback policy: current config tries smaller model when latency breaches 500ms per-token. in this incident it triggered because cache misses spiked. we can change to: only fallback after N consecutive token failures or if queue depth exceeds threshold. that'll reduce oscillation.

[16:05] Priya: yes, oscillation is scary. can you include a canary config for fallback? we need a safe ramp to ensure quality doesn't degrade.

[16:30] Diego: canary: route 1% of traffic to fallback policy for 2 hours, monitor quality regressions on sample prompts, then 5% for 4 hours, etc. we'll include auto-rollback if quality metric delta > 2%.

[17:15] Marcus: about quality metrics - we need reproducible evals and a set of prompts to watch. we'll share our prompt set and acceptance thresholds.

[17:50] Liam: i'll share the prompt set plus example failures.

[18:20] Samira: great. pricing and procurement: Samira to send a pilot quote for a 3-week Dedicated pool + benching support.

[19:00] Priya: legal timeline: we need 2 weeks to route procurement. if bench starts 4/27 and readout 5/5 that's tight but doable.

[19:35] Samira: we'll aim to align.

[20:00] (brief mute/unmuting sounds)

[20:30] Diego: technical deep dive note - kernel mis-selection can be triggered when sequence-length hist changes rapidly. two mitigations: add sequence-length aware routing or force runtime to prefer smaller kernels for short sequences. both have cost tradeoffs.

[21:10] Liam: what's the perf hit of forcing kernels?

[21:20] Diego: ~5-12% token throughput loss in worst case but reduces tail dramatically. for pilot we can accept that to validate.

[22:05] Priya: can Redwood's runtime surface kernel selection metrics? we need to see which kernels ran.

[22:20] Diego: yes we'll include kernel traces in the bench output - note: sometimes names are obfuscated in our internal logs; we'll map them.

[23:00] Marcus: encryption rotation: we need a KMS rotation schedule and proof that keys are never exfiltrated. how do you log key access?

[23:25] Samira: access to KMS calls is logged with audit entries and we can provide those logs; for private deployments you control your own KMS/HSM and Redwood integrates via KMIP or cloud KMS. we'll add HSM note to the security pack.

[24:10] Liam: can we get an architecture diagram for Dedicated + VPC peering + control plane callbacks?

[24:25] Diego: yes i'll attach a diagram. recommend isolating control plane egress to a small set of IPs and using mutual TLS for control-plane webhooks.

[25:00] Priya: what about data residency - some of our data must stay in EU. do you have regional Dedicated pools?

[25:20] Samira: yes we have EU regions and can pin the pilot to eu-west1. we'll include region-level SLA notes.

[26:05] (background keyboard typing)

[26:40] Liam: regarding the log ingestion blip, we'll add redundancy to our forwarder. that's on our backlog; we'll reprioritize if it's a gating factor.

[27:00] Samira: ok next: we want to document the postmortem for transparency. who owns the doc?

[27:20] Liam: i can own primary write-up, Marcus and Priya will add security and platform notes, and Samira will add Redwood mitigations and timeline.

[27:50] Samira: perfect. please include the decision log for fallback config changes.

[28:30] Diego: small FYI: sometimes transcribed logs call it 'KV cash' or 'runtime privet' in the auto-transcripts - ignore those typos in the shared raw logs, they are just transcription artifacts.

[29:10] Priya: (laugh) noted.

[30:00] Samira: ok to recap: bench plan kickoff 4/27, Redwood shares security pack and connectivity checklist, OzoneBank provides traces and prompt set, pilot quote by 4/26, follow-up readout 5/5. Anything else?

[30:40] Liam: we also requested a small config change: adjust fallback threshold and add 1-minute cool-off to avoid oscillation.

[31:10] Diego: noted - will propose exact config and include canary steps.

[31:45] Marcus: legal: we'll need an NDA addendum for the pilot specifics. procurement team will send the contact.

[32:10] Samira: I'll coordinate with legal and get that out.

[33:00] Priya: last Q: if Dedicated pilot shows improvement, what's the lift to move to Private on-prem later?

[33:25] Samira: depends on integrations - Private requires network controls and a deployment window; typical lift is 6-12 weeks for air-gapped on-prem, less for VPC-based private control planes. we'll provide a migration checklist.

[34:00] Diego: technical note - prefix stickiness is a cheap mitigation: route same prefix to same inference pool to improve cache hit rate. it can be implemented in a week for pilot.

[34:35] Liam: do that and include metrics we'll watch.

[35:00] (agreement noises)

[35:30] Samira: ok action recap: Diego bench+config, Samira security+pricing, Liam traces+prompt set, Priya procurement timeline. we'll sync on 4/27 bench kickoff.

[36:10] (short silence, clicking)

[36:40] Diego: one more thing - fallback logs must capture the exact prefix and last-known KV state to aid repro. that'll require a small change to the request logger but it's low risk.

[37:10] Marcus: sounds good, make sure access to those logs is RBAC-gated.

[37:40] Samira: yes, RBAC will be applied.

[38:20] Priya: can you also provide an estimated cost delta for enabling sequence-length aware routing vs kernel forcing? we need to compare cost vs reliability.

[38:40] Diego: i'll add a cost estimate to the bench report - rough numbers now: sequence-aware routing +3-6% cost, kernel forcing +5-12% cost.

[39:15] Liam: if we can trade 6% cost for a 50% reduction in tail lat that's worth it.

[40:00] Samira: noted.

[40:30] (phone notifications)

[41:00] Diego: last logistical note: we'll push the bench results spreadsheet to the shared drive and tag the runs with a unique run id. please keep that id in followups.

[41:30] Liam: agreed.

[42:00] Samira: ok any final questions?

[42:20] Priya: none from me.

[42:35] Marcus: no.

[43:00] Samira: thanks everyone. i'll send the deck and security pack after this call, and Diego will post the bench plan. see you at bench kickoff 4/27.

[43:30] (goodbyes)

[44:00] End of recording.
